correctness.rationale: Every paired-dominating set in a bipartite graph selects equally many vertices on both shores. With s>=2 on each shore, deleting a matching removes at most one neighbor per vertex, so the selected set dominates. Hall’s condition holds since a singleton selected vertex sees at least s-1>=1 selected opposite vertices, while every subset of two or more selected vertices sees the entire selected opposite shore. For s=1, any endpoint touched by a deleted edge causes either an absent selected edge or one undominated omitted partner; untouched endpoints are sufficient. Independent binomial counting yields the all-set polynomial, Vandermonde yields its total, and rook inclusion-exclusion yields the exact pairing-weighted coefficients. An independent brute-force graph-neighborhood and perfect-matching verifier checks every vertex subset for all m,n from two to six and all possible matching deletion sizes.

originality.rationale: The all-t deleted-matching stability and paired-set-matching counting theorem was not located in targeted published-finding corpus and literature searches. The published complete-multipartite paired-domination polynomial covers only the t=0 biclique, while the chain-graph result does not apply after deleting at least two matching edges, which induce a 2K2. Earlier crown-specific sources already state gamma_pr=4 and are credited as covering that scalar endpoint; neither inspected original crown source gives the all-size polynomial or matching multiplicities. An older 2016 generic polynomial contribution is accessible only as a one-page abstract, a genuine residual originality risk, not proof of absence.
residual_risks: The 2016 generic paired-domination-polynomial conference item was available only as a one-page abstract; unspecified standard families could include a previously published matching-deletion special case.
The recent cubic bipartite paper was read at abstract level only, although its stated cubic theorem is not directly relevant to dense matching-deleted bicliques.
Matching-deleted bicliques have alternate names (crown graphs when balanced and fully deleted; almost complete bipartite graphs generally), and differently worded work may escape search.
Neither search nor graph-family partition establishes absolute priority.

value.rationale: The motivating question is edge-fault tolerance of paired domination: vertex placements should dominate and admit distinct backup pairings even after disjoint communication links fail. The theorem identifies a sharp robustness threshold—every 2s-set with s>=2 survives every matching deletion, and only size-two feasibility changes—then provides complete coefficients and a separate exact measure of how many pairing options remain. This is a natural all-parameter structural result, not a single scalar crown computation; both the deletion-invariant set spectrum and the rook-counted witness spectrum are potentially useful for fault-tolerant matching and paired-domination studies.
